checklist.name: Claim form – Part A (signed by you)
Claim form – Part B (filled by hospital)
checklist.why: The hospital confirms the treatment details

checklist.name: Discharge summary
checklist.source: Ward or billing desk at discharge
checklist.why: Shows the diagnosis and treatment given

checklist.name: Final itemised bill
checklist.why: Every charge must be listed separately

checklist.name: Payment receipts
checklist.source: Hospital billing desk – ask for a receipt for each payment

checklist.name: Investigation reports (blood tests, ultrasound)
checklist.why: Supports the diagnosis in the discharge summary

checklist.name: Cancelled cheque or bank details
checklist.why: So the insurer can pay you

checklist.name: Hospital note on room availability
checklist.why: Shows whether a room within your ₹5,000/day limit was available – helps challenge the room-rent cut

checklist.name: Itemised explanation of the ₹9,500
checklist.source: Insurer – request it with the letter
checklist.why: The settlement letter gives no reason for this amount

escalation.name: Insurer's grievance cell
escalation.when: First step. Write to the insurer with your questions and evidence.
escalation.howTo: Use the grievance email or form on the insurer's website. Note the reference number.

escalation.name: Bima Bharosa (IRDAI)
escalation.when: If the insurer does not reply in time, or you disagree with the reply.
escalation.howTo: Register the complaint online on the IRDAI Bima Bharosa portal.

escalation.name: Insurance Ombudsman
escalation.when: If it is still unresolved. There is a time limit after the insurer's final reply – check it before filing.
escalation.howTo: File with the Ombudsman office for your area.
